title: Design Patterns in Ruby
intro: Design pattern questions in Ruby interviews are really about recognising when a Rails app's models are doing too much and knowing which pattern extracts the right responsibility. Service objects extract business logic from fat models (SRP). Form objects handle multi-model forms or complex validation scenarios. Query objects encapsulate complex ActiveRecord query logic. Value objects represent domain values with equality semantics (Money, EmailAddress). Decorators extend objects without subclassing. This page covers SOLID applied to Ruby (with the insight that in Ruby, Strategy is just passing a Proc), the five patterns Rails engineers reach for most, SimpleDelegator as a lightweight decorator, and the decision between a service object and a concern — the answer depends on whether the logic is shared and whether it involves external I/O.
